Existing interventions

Wholemeal rye bread in place of the tested refined wheat bread

The result applies to the tested breads and does not identify one responsible nutrient.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-1

Fish before rice in the studied meal sequence

An acute meal result; no claim that protein alone accounts for the effect.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-2

The tested high-slowly-digestible-starch breakfast in place of extruded cereal

Measured in 12 tracer participants after specific breakfasts; no universal product, dose or longer-term outcome claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-3

The studied whey preload before a carbohydrate meal

Eight adults with diet-controlled type 2 diabetes; 55 g whey 30 min before the meal, additional energy, acute results. No universal preload prescription or direct requirement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-4

The tested semolina pasta matrix in place of semolina bread or couscous

Separate human and simulated-digestion experiments; appearance slowing is inferred, not quantified. The result does not apply to every pasta or processing method.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-5

Cooling and reheating the tested chickpea pasta

Twelve healthy adults; 24 h at 4 °C and the tested reheating method. Glucose entry was not measured and digestible carbohydrate was not re-matched after processing.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-6

The tested beta-glucan addition to a polenta meal

Twelve overweight adults; no lower overall appearing quantity and no universal fibre effect. Viscosity is a proposed explanation, not a measured mediator.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-7

The tested guar–chickpea flour flatbread blend

The primary half-absorption-time endpoint did not change significantly; larger liver-production and disposal changes also occurred. No isolated guar effect or general fibre requirement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-8

Isomaltulose instead of sucrose in the studied sugar-load comparison

Eleven adults with type 2 diabetes under a clamp; not an instruction to add sugar. A separate 12-week trial did not show an HbA1c advantage.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-9

Vinegar with the studied starchy meal

Indirect marker in ten healthy volunteers, no appearance flux. Further delay occurred in diabetic gastroparesis and may be disadvantageous; do not apply this practice to that context.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-10

Less-processed whole-grain food package (two-week trial)

A food package, not an isolated grain or fibre effect; unmasked foods, short duration. Concealed randomisation, blinded CGM, initial masked analysis and intention-to-treat models support appraisal.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM2-SOP-2

Early eating with front-loaded calories (six-day trial)

Small sample, no washout; timing, eating-window length and calorie distribution cannot be separated.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM2-SOP-3

Supervised interval walking (two-week trial)

Small unmasked trial, baseline imbalance and missing sensor record; oxidative-stress markers did not improve. No blanket superiority to all continuous exercise.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM2-LIFE-2

Four brief vigorous activity bouts daily (48-hour trial)

Small secondary effects without multiplicity adjustment; short washout permits carryover. Not evidence for gentle walking or lasting clinical benefit.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM2-LIFE-3

Diet-induced weight reduction when excess adiposity is relevant

This is conditional on the studied metabolic context, not a general recommendation to lose weight.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM3-SOP-1

Conditional oral arginine supplementation in the tested type-2-diabetes protocol

Incomplete normalisation; small selected clinical population. cGMP change does not isolate causal NO mediation. The 9 g/day supplement protocol is not equivalent to arginine-containing food.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM3-SOP-DEFERRED-1

Six-hour early eating window with weight-maintenance feeding

OGTT-derived index, not clamp disposal, tissue signalling or a directly measured circadian mechanism. Fasting and OGTT glucose unchanged; hs-CRP, IL-6 and cortisol unchanged. Eight male completers, unmasked supervised efficacy trial; four withdrawals. Eating-window duration and early timing coupled; pretest fast unmatched. Sequence/period effects affected some other outcomes, not the selected index. Fasting triglycerides and total cholesterol increased; not a uniformly beneficial metabolic profile. Highly supervised protocol does not establish general feasibility or an unsupervised fasting prescription.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM3-SOP-EARLY-EATING-1

Regular aerobic activity (studied training)

Short type 2 diabetes experiment; long-term magnitude and individual responses vary.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM3-LIFE-1

Aligned sleep–wake and meal scheduling

Restoring every abnormal rhythm and the separate contribution of each cue were not tested.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm2/brs6-fm2-pm4-cortisol-rhythm-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM4-SOP-1

Focused-attention meditation after an acute stressor

Acute student sample; HRV recovery was not unique to meditation.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm6-sympathetic-activation-and-parasympathetic-recovery.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM6-SOP-1

Six minutes of app-guided Papworth–Benson diaphragmatic breathing with heart-wave feedback versus passive control or rumination after a laboratory speech stressor.

No verified six-breaths/minute prescription; remove that preliminary-discovery shorthand. Table 1 does not show significant HF difference versus passive control; narrative overgeneralisation is not adopted. Monitoring ended after six minutes; breathing itself affects HRV. Developer employees authored study; editorial notice flags nonregistration. No cardiovascular-disease prevention claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm6-sympathetic-activation-and-parasympathetic-recovery.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM6-LP-GUIDED-BREATHING-1

Slow-paced breathing at six cycles per minute

Session HRV is respiration-dependent and does not show durable whole-body vagal improvement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm7-vagal-tone-hrv-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM7-SOP-1

EPA+DHA supplementation (studied combined formulation)

Small elevated-triglyceride sample; no separated EPA/DHA necessity or routine benefit claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm7-vagal-tone-hrv-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM7-SOP-2

Aerobic conditioning in the tested twelve-week programme

Sex-dependent findings, respiration/context-sensitive cardiac proxy, not direct whole-body vagal traffic or universal recovery improvement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm7-vagal-tone-hrv-regulation.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM7-LP-DEFERRED-1

Hypocaloric dietary weight-loss programme in adults with obesity

Studied 10–20-week programmes and multiphase follow-up predominantly involved women with obesity. Energy restriction, weight loss and co-interventions are not independently separable. Ex vivo release is not whole-body flux; lower leptin is not a universal goal and adiponectin did not consistently increase. No food-specific effect, individual caloric target or brain benefit is inferred.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm4/brs6-fm4-pm8-metabolic-inflammation-and-adipose-stress-signalling.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM8-SOP-1

Milled flaxseed in the studied balanced-diet protocol

30 g/day for 12 weeks is the tested protocol, not a universal effective dose. Differential dropout, concurrent weight change and pooled null/heterogeneous adiponectin evidence limit generalisation. No isolated ALA/lignan/fibre, secretion or brain claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm4/brs6-fm4-pm8-metabolic-inflammation-and-adipose-stress-signalling.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM8-SOP-2

Aerobic exercise with context-specific adipose endocrine responses

Interstitial concentration is not secretion rate; transcripts are not released protein or receptor sensitivity. Acute and chronic protocols, sex, adiposity and weight change differ; one training study found no tissue-transcript change. No universal dose, optimal hormone direction or brain/clinical benefit established.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm4/brs6-fm4-pm8-metabolic-inflammation-and-adipose-stress-signalling.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM8-LL-1

Food-related mindfulness training

Self-report and pseudo-randomized allocation; neural mediation and real-world intake remain unproven.

Fish before rice in the studied meal sequence

An acute meal result; no claim that protein alone accounts for the effect.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-2

The tested high-slowly-digestible-starch breakfast in place of extruded cereal

Measured in 12 tracer participants after specific breakfasts; no universal product, dose or longer-term outcome claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-3

The studied whey preload before a carbohydrate meal

Eight adults with diet-controlled type 2 diabetes; 55 g whey 30 min before the meal, additional energy, acute results. No universal preload prescription or direct requirement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-4

The tested semolina pasta matrix in place of semolina bread or couscous

Separate human and simulated-digestion experiments; appearance slowing is inferred, not quantified. The result does not apply to every pasta or processing method.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-5

Cooling and reheating the tested chickpea pasta

Twelve healthy adults; 24 h at 4 °C and the tested reheating method. Glucose entry was not measured and digestible carbohydrate was not re-matched after processing.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-6

The tested beta-glucan addition to a polenta meal

Twelve overweight adults; no lower overall appearing quantity and no universal fibre effect. Viscosity is a proposed explanation, not a measured mediator.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-7

The tested guar–chickpea flour flatbread blend

The primary half-absorption-time endpoint did not change significantly; larger liver-production and disposal changes also occurred. No isolated guar effect or general fibre requirement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-8

Isomaltulose instead of sucrose in the studied sugar-load comparison

Eleven adults with type 2 diabetes under a clamp; not an instruction to add sugar. A separate 12-week trial did not show an HbA1c advantage.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-9

Vinegar with the studied starchy meal

Indirect marker in ten healthy volunteers, no appearance flux. Further delay occurred in diabetic gastroparesis and may be disadvantageous; do not apply this practice to that context.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm1-glucose-appearance-kinetics.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM1-SOP-10

Less-processed whole-grain food package (two-week trial)

A food package, not an isolated grain or fibre effect; unmasked foods, short duration. Concealed randomisation, blinded CGM, initial masked analysis and intention-to-treat models support appraisal.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM2-SOP-2

Early eating with front-loaded calories (six-day trial)

Small sample, no washout; timing, eating-window length and calorie distribution cannot be separated.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM2-SOP-3

Supervised interval walking (two-week trial)

Small unmasked trial, baseline imbalance and missing sensor record; oxidative-stress markers did not improve. No blanket superiority to all continuous exercise.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM2-LIFE-2

Four brief vigorous activity bouts daily (48-hour trial)

Small secondary effects without multiplicity adjustment; short washout permits carryover. Not evidence for gentle walking or lasting clinical benefit.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm2-glycaemic-variability-regulation.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM2-LIFE-3

Diet-induced weight reduction when excess adiposity is relevant

This is conditional on the studied metabolic context, not a general recommendation to lose weight.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM3-SOP-1

Conditional oral arginine supplementation in the tested type-2-diabetes protocol

Incomplete normalisation; small selected clinical population. cGMP change does not isolate causal NO mediation. The 9 g/day supplement protocol is not equivalent to arginine-containing food.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM3-SOP-DEFERRED-1

Six-hour early eating window with weight-maintenance feeding

OGTT-derived index, not clamp disposal, tissue signalling or a directly measured circadian mechanism. Fasting and OGTT glucose unchanged; hs-CRP, IL-6 and cortisol unchanged. Eight male completers, unmasked supervised efficacy trial; four withdrawals. Eating-window duration and early timing coupled; pretest fast unmatched. Sequence/period effects affected some other outcomes, not the selected index. Fasting triglycerides and total cholesterol increased; not a uniformly beneficial metabolic profile. Highly supervised protocol does not establish general feasibility or an unsupervised fasting prescription.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM3-SOP-EARLY-EATING-1

Regular aerobic activity (studied training)

Short type 2 diabetes experiment; long-term magnitude and individual responses vary.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm1/brs6-fm1-pm3-insulin-sensitivity-and-glucose-disposal.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM3-LIFE-1

Aligned sleep–wake and meal scheduling

Restoring every abnormal rhythm and the separate contribution of each cue were not tested.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm2/brs6-fm2-pm4-cortisol-rhythm-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM4-SOP-1

Focused-attention meditation after an acute stressor

Acute student sample; HRV recovery was not unique to meditation.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm6-sympathetic-activation-and-parasympathetic-recovery.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM6-SOP-1

Six minutes of app-guided Papworth–Benson diaphragmatic breathing with heart-wave feedback versus passive control or rumination after a laboratory speech stressor.

No verified six-breaths/minute prescription; remove that preliminary-discovery shorthand. Table 1 does not show significant HF difference versus passive control; narrative overgeneralisation is not adopted. Monitoring ended after six minutes; breathing itself affects HRV. Developer employees authored study; editorial notice flags nonregistration. No cardiovascular-disease prevention claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm6-sympathetic-activation-and-parasympathetic-recovery.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM6-LP-GUIDED-BREATHING-1

Slow-paced breathing at six cycles per minute

Session HRV is respiration-dependent and does not show durable whole-body vagal improvement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm7-vagal-tone-hrv-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM7-SOP-1

EPA+DHA supplementation (studied combined formulation)

Small elevated-triglyceride sample; no separated EPA/DHA necessity or routine benefit claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm7-vagal-tone-hrv-regulation.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM7-SOP-2

Aerobic conditioning in the tested twelve-week programme

Sex-dependent findings, respiration/context-sensitive cardiac proxy, not direct whole-body vagal traffic or universal recovery improvement.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm3/brs6-fm3-pm7-vagal-tone-hrv-regulation.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM7-LP-DEFERRED-1

Hypocaloric dietary weight-loss programme in adults with obesity

Studied 10–20-week programmes and multiphase follow-up predominantly involved women with obesity. Energy restriction, weight loss and co-interventions are not independently separable. Ex vivo release is not whole-body flux; lower leptin is not a universal goal and adiponectin did not consistently increase. No food-specific effect, individual caloric target or brain benefit is inferred.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm4/brs6-fm4-pm8-metabolic-inflammation-and-adipose-stress-signalling.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM8-SOP-1

Milled flaxseed in the studied balanced-diet protocol

30 g/day for 12 weeks is the tested protocol, not a universal effective dose. Differential dropout, concurrent weight change and pooled null/heterogeneous adiponectin evidence limit generalisation. No isolated ALA/lignan/fibre, secretion or brain claim.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm4/brs6-fm4-pm8-metabolic-inflammation-and-adipose-stress-signalling.mdx#system_optimisation_practices/PM8-SOP-2

Aerobic exercise with context-specific adipose endocrine responses

Interstitial concentration is not secretion rate; transcripts are not released protein or receptor sensitivity. Acute and chronic protocols, sex, adiposity and weight change differ; one training study found no tissue-transcript change. No universal dose, optimal hormone direction or brain/clinical benefit established.

docs/biological-targets/brs6/fm4/brs6-fm4-pm8-metabolic-inflammation-and-adipose-stress-signalling.mdx#lifestyle_priorities/PM8-LL-1

Food-related mindfulness training

Self-report and pseudo-randomized allocation; neural mediation and real-world intake remain unproven.
